title: Knowledge-Guided Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization
source_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Core finite-dimensional reformulations independently verified; unconditional out-of-sample interpretation, local proof formulas, and empirical prose/plot inconsistencies need correction.
limitations: No available relevant author repository; no author execution or full experimental reproduction.
Separate OpenReview attachments unavailable; bibliography and later errata not audited.
General population guarantees and empirical significance not established.

problems.evidence: N=1 sample (e1,1), theta=e1: unique robust optimizer e1 has robust risk zero, but true law equal mass (e1,1),(e2,1) gives risk .5.
problems.assumptions: d=2,delta>0,rank Theta=1; sample occurs with probability .5.
problems.counterevidence: Proposition itself valid inside ambiguity set; conclusion explicitly defers statistical guarantees.
problems.repair: Qualify guarantee by population membership; distinguish collinearity from equality to theta.
problems.core_dependency: Interpretation; central algebraic reformulations remain valid.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read cost definitions and Proposition3.1 interpretation pp.4â€“5, its proof p.13 and future-statistical-guarantees statement p.9. Strong transport preserves (Y,theta^TX); no population-membership assumption is stated. The two-dimensional example has rankTheta=1<d, delta>0, N=1.
independent_check.decisive_check: Independently minimized |1-beta1|+sqrt(delta)|beta2|: unique optimum(1,0), zero robust and empirical adapter risk. Under equal population mass on(e1,1),(e2,1), the observed sample occurs with probability1/2 and true risk is1/2. The theta^TX marginal changes from all1 to half0/half1, so no radius permits population membership.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Choosing beta=alpha*theta proves the proposition's restricted-set statement directly without minimax interchange. Interpreting 'out-of-sample' solely inside the specified ambiguity set rescues it; the report correctly limits its objection to an unconditional population interpretation. Statistical guarantees are explicitly future work, so this is a Minor scope correction rather than a failed central statistical theorem.
independent_check.result: Supported Minor. Collinearity means membership in spanTheta, not equality to theta or unrestricted immunity to negative transfer.

problems.evidence: Actual quadratic supremum 1 versus printed radial supremum 0; negative logistic conjugate has domain [-1,0], not [0,1]; weighted signed linear penalty can be unbounded.

problems.repair: Correct residual, radial cross-term sign, squared thresholds, conjugate sign, weighted quadratic norm, endpoint cases and conjugacy qualification.
